## Findings
- claim-1: For \(p,c\ge1\), hence in particular for \(\min(p,c)=1\), \[ I_{j+c,i+p}\subseteq I_{j+1,i+1}. \]
- claim-2: The induced quotient map restricts surjectively as \[ J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow J_{1,1}, \] and induces a surjection \[ Q_{p,c}=J_{p,c}/\Lambda_+J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow J_{1,1}/\Lambda_+J_{1,1}=Q_{1,1}. \]
## Strategy
Let \(B_{r,q}=\{\lambda:\lambda\subseteq q^r\}\). By the Schur-basis definition,
\[
I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\notin B_{r,q}}\mathbb Zs_\lambda .
\]
Since \(p,c\ge1\),
\[
(i+1)^{j+1}\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}.
\]
Thus \(B_{j+1,i+1}\subseteq B_{j+c,i+p}\), so their complements satisfy
\[
I_{j+c,i+p}\subseteq I_{j+1,i+1}.
\]
This proves the requested inclusion (indeed, for all \(p,c\ge1\), not only \(\min(p,c)=1\)).

Hence there is a quotient map
\[
\phi:\Lambda/I_{j+c,i+p}\twoheadrightarrow\Lambda/I_{j+1,i+1}.
\]
Under the Schur-basis interval definition of \(J_{p,c}\), \(\phi\) fixes each class \(s_\mu\) with
\[
i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1},
\]
and these classes span \(J_{1,1}\). They are also classes in \(J_{p,c}\). Therefore
\[
\phi(J_{p,c})=J_{1,1},
\]
so \(\phi\) restricts to a surjection
\[
J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow J_{1,1}.
\]

Finally \(\phi\) is \(\Lambda\)-linear, whence
\[
\phi(\Lambda_+J_{p,c})=\Lambda_+\phi(J_{p,c})
=\Lambda_+J_{1,1}.
\]
It therefore induces a surjection
\[
Q_{p,c}=J_{p,c}/\Lambda_+J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow
J_{1,1}/\Lambda_+J_{1,1}=Q_{1,1}.
\]

Thus the requested target is established directly from the Schur-basis box and interval definitions.

## Gaps
No additional hypothesis beyond the stated Schur-basis definitions is used. This is a direct formal argument, not external source-backed grounding.
